subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Op-Amps: The Swiss Army Knife of Electronics
description: A quick win: understand Op-Amps: The Swiss Army Knife of Electronics.

hook.text: An operational amplifier costs 10 cents and does everything: amplify, filter, compare, and compute.

buildup.text: An op-amp has two inputs and one output. It amplifies the difference between the inputs by a huge factor.

discovery.text: Negative feedback tames the gain. By connecting output to input through a resistor, you get precise, controllable amplification.

twist.text: The original op-amp filled a room and cost $1,000 in 1941. The LM741, introduced in 1968, costs pennies.

climax.text: Audio equipment, medical instruments, and control systems all depend on op-amps. They're in virtually every analog circuit.

punchline.text: Two inputs, one output, infinite uses. The op-amp does it all.

quiz.question: How does negative feedback improve an operational amplifier?
options: It increases the op-amp's maximum output voltage range
It provides precise, controllable amplification by taming the raw gain
It reduces the power consumption of the amplifier circuit
